newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT - Morgan Stanley ups UK stock rating.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Morgan Stanley ups UK stock rating.

text.p: UK stocks were raised to "overweight" from "neutral" at Morgan Stanley, equity strategist Richard Davidson at the brokerage said on Tuesday.

Davidson said prospects for most leading European equity markets in 1997 were poor against a background of an expected recovery in economic growth and upward pressure on interest rates, yet the UK looked better value than most.

He said the UK's FTSE 100 had recently underperformed other leading markets yet through 1997, he expected it to outperform other indexes in Morgan Stanley's model portfolio of European equity markets.
He said risks of rising UK interest rates and of a windfall tax on utilities had already been discounted while the positive aspects of strong growth had not yet been recognised.

Davidson said he expected the UK economy to expand by 3.8 percent in 1997, translating into 15 percent growth in company earnings per share -- well above the consensus expectation of 8.5 percent growth.
UK shares were trading on around 12 times expected 1997 earnings and around 8.2 times 1997 cashflow, the Morgan Stanley strategist said, making the market look relatively good value.

He said Morgan Stanley had raised its weighting on the FTSE 100 to "neutral" from "underweight" in July, and had now further raised its weighting on the UK market to 37 percent compared with a "neutral" stance of 34 percent.
